-98.49220,29.61530.name: Aspire Fertility-San Antonio
-98.49220,29.61530.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Ursula Balthazar, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-85.49598,32.59195.name: College of Veterinary Medicine, College of Agriculture and Harrison College of Pharmacy
-85.49598,32.59195.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Auburn University. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-81.27480,43.00542.name: Western University
-81.27480,43.00542.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, November 2024
-81.27480,43.00542.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, November 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-51.93000,-14.24000.desc: Clinics report to a national system run by the medical regulator, but clinic-level data is not published.

-51.93000,-14.24000.name: Brazil — no public facility register
-51.93000,-14.24000.desc: Institutions register with a national council and aggregate figures exist, but facility-level inspection records are not published.

113.97000,22.59000.name: BGI Group
113.97000,22.59000.desc: The largest genomics organisation in the world by sequencing capacity, based in Shenzhen, and the subject of sustained Western government concern about where the genetic data it processes ends up. Read alongside the US and European companies on this map, every large genomic operation accumulates human data and every one of them is trusted or distrusted according to its flag rather than its practices.

-78.89860,35.99400.name: Thermo Fisher — Patheon and clinical services
-78.89860,35.99400.desc: Thermo Fisher's contract manufacturing and clinical trial arms, added by acquisition. The company supplying the instruments, the reagents, the manufacturing and the trial services is one company.

-78.89860,35.99400.name: GBIRd — Genetic Biocontrol of Invasive Rodents
-78.89860,35.99400.desc: A partnership developing gene-drive mice to clear invasive rodents from islands. Islands are chosen because a drive should stay put, but mice reach islands on boats, which is how they arrived — so the containment argument rests on the same transport that defeated it before.

35.03400,32.78800.name: Aleph Farms
35.03400,32.78800.desc: Received the first regulatory approval anywhere for cultivated beef, in Israel in 2024, and has applied in Switzerland, the UK and Thailand. Beef matters more than chicken here: it is the meat with the largest land and methane footprint, so it is the one the environmental argument for this technology rests on.
